name: add
note: review: Only corelibs-operator-first-step-wins is listed, which pins numberAdd only when binary_op1 answers; the NotImplemented branch of PyNumber_Add (sq_concat, then the '+' TypeError, Objects/abstract.c:1138-1154) and binary_op1's slot order are unpinned, so a numberAdd that ignores sq_concat passes; sequence-fallback (pyFns has add) and binary-dispatch (pyFns lacks add) are not listed.

name: index
note: review: indexPy (Proto.lean:420-429) answers PyLong_Check before the type's __index__, but `a.__index__()` (:97) is an attribute lookup that finds an int subclass's own __index__: for `class I(int): __index__ = lambda s: 7`, the pure twin returns 7 and C returns 3, while IndexExact's clause `o.inst = none -> o.isInt = some n -> indexPy o = .ok (.exact n)` says 3, so the proven statement is false about CPython (and the twin difference is not on record in corelibs-operator-twin-corners).

name: mul
note: review: Only first-step-wins is listed, which pins numberMul only when binary_op1 answers; the sq_repeat branches of PyNumber_Multiply (left then right repeat, the count through __index__, its OverflowError, the '*' TypeError) and binary_op1's order are unpinned, so a numberMul that never repeats passes; sequence-fallback and binary-dispatch are not listed.

name: pow
note: review: Only first-step-wins is listed, which pins numberPow only when binary_op1 answers; the NotImplemented case (the 'unsupported operand type(s) for ** or pow()' TypeError) and binary_op1's order are unpinned, so a numberPow returning any other error passes; corelibs-operator-power (pyFns has pow) and binary-dispatch are not listed.

name: concat
note: review: ConcatArgs.hasGetitem is a plain Bool, so `hasattr(a, '__getitem__')` (:156) cannot raise, but hasattr propagates any exception other than AttributeError from a __getattribute__, __getattr__ or descriptor, which the pure twin then raises where C says \"can't be concatenated\"; the rest (message from type(a).__name__, then `a + b` as nb_add then sq_concat) is mirrored and pinned by ConcatExact.

name: contains
note: review: Only search-exact is listed, and SearchExact never gives containsOp a slot and pins only non-TypeError iter failures, so the __contains__ branch of PySequence_Contains (`b in a`, Objects/abstract.c:2240-2250) and the 'is not a container or iterable' rewrite are unpinned; corelibs-operator-iter-errors pins both and names contains, but the row does not list it.

name: length_hint
note: review: lengthHintPy follows :202-230 in order, but the lookup `type(obj).__length_hint__` (:212-215) cannot fail in the model (a descriptor's __get__(None, cls) or a metaclass __getattr__ raising anything but AttributeError propagates), and it also finds a __length_hint__ defined on the metaclass, which C's _PyObject_LookupSpecial (Objects/typeobject.c:2990-3002) never reads, so LengthHintPyExact's `o.hint = none -> .ok d` is false for such a class; the default and val are also returned as the objects given (length_hint(object(), True) is True in Python, 1 in C) and `val < 0` (:227) runs an int subclass's __lt__, all merged into Int.

name: attrgetter.__init__
note: review: No listed theorem pins a rejection by attrgetterNewPy: AttrNameExact fixes namePy .other only and AttrCallExact only acceptance, so an attrgetterNewPy that accepts a non-str passes (corelibs-operator-attrgetter-rejects pins :252-253 and :263 but is not listed); and AttrArg.strSub carries a Chain, so a str subclass whose `split('.')` (:255) raises or returns non-str items cannot be expressed.

name: attrgetter.__repr__
note: review: AttrReprExact only equates attrReprC with reprPy (plus dotjoin facts and C's guard), which two equally wrong repr functions would also satisfy, so the text of :272-274 and its first failing repr are not pinned by the listed entries; GetterReprExact pins reprPy itself but names only itemgetter in its pyFns and is not listed here.

name: attrgetter.__reduce__
note: review: The only listed entry, attr-name-exact, says nothing about the Python __reduce__ (attrArgsPy, Getters.lean:223-226, appears in no listed theorem), and attrArgsPy turns `self._attrs` into characters, dropping the objects the body returns; the body returns one field with no branch, so a `trivial:` exclusion or a round trip through attrgetterNewPy is what is missing.

name: itemgetter.__reduce__
note: review: The Python half of ItemgetterReduce is `igReducePy args = args`, rfl on the identity (IgReduce.lean:50), which any function returning its input satisfies, and the round trip is stated for C only; IgReduce.lean:48-49 cites :291 and :297 for where _items is set, which are :289 and :294; the body returns one field with no branch, so `trivial:` would fit.

name: methodcaller.__repr__
note: review: mcReprPy takes keywords as List (String x a), but `'%s' % k` (:332) is str(k), which for a str-subclass key (kept by **kwargs) runs its __str__, which may print something else or raise, where C formats %U (Modules/_operator.c:1838); and a value's repr that changes `self._kwargs` makes the items() iteration raise RuntimeError, which a list cannot express; McReprOrder is otherwise a sound pin of the name-first order.

name: methodcaller.__reduce__
note: review: mcReduce has no failure path, but `from functools import partial` (:341) can raise and partial(...) raises TypeError for a Placeholder keyword value, as McReduceExact pins for C; and MethodcallerNew's round trip also holds for a reduce that always takes the partial branch, so the `if not self._kwargs` branch (:338) is unpinned.

name: iconcat
note: review: Same gap as concat: `hasattr(a, '__getitem__')` (:359) is a Bool in the model and cannot propagate the non-AttributeError exception that hasattr passes on; the `a += b` part is mirrored as plusEq and pinned by ConcatExact.
